what_happened: Phase 7's first deploy-headless.sh run reported 3 of 41 checks failed: skills/skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md over its measure-eager-context.sh byte ceiling (zero headroom pre-existing; task 620 had trimmed it to exactly fit before this task's own Phase 4 addition pushed it over), one shellcheck SC2034 in the new test suite, and lint-subject-resolution-declaration.sh flagging THREE test suites (two -- test-suite-resolver-lib.sh, test-unmapped-fallback-lib.sh -- never touched by this plan at all) calling the legacy common_test_resolve_candidate with no explicit mode. All three pre-dated this task; the two unrelated suites were introduced together in a prior commit and never caught because no orchestration had closed on the full gate set since -- a direct, concrete illustration of the exact defect class this task fixes. Fixed forward: SKILL.md's own addition relocated to batch-gate-stage.md (byte-identical-to-baseline), the shellcheck finding resolved with an inline disable, and all three suites migrated to common_test_resolve_subject + common_test_declare_subject. Second deploy-headless.sh run: RESULT=landed_verify_clean, 41/41.

This task's own closing battery, run for the first time at Phase 7, caught two genuine pre-existing defects in the repository (one lint violation across two unrelated test suites, never previously caught) purely because this was the first time the complete gate set had ever run as a closing step rather than being individually deferred/skipped by each task. Direct, unplanned validation that the mechanism this task builds does what it is meant to do.
